0.name: Pepper_bell___Bacterial_spot
0.symptoms: Small, water-soaked, dark spots appear on leaves, often with a yellow halo, and may merge into larger irregular lesions. Spots can also appear on fruit.
recommended_actions: Remove and destroy severely affected leaves
Avoid overhead watering and working in fields when leaves are wet
Ensure good spacing between plants for airflow
Rotate crops in future seasons
Follow locally approved plant-protection guidance

1.name: Pepper_bell___healthy

2.name: Potato___Early_blight
2.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings appear, typically on older leaves first.
recommended_actions: Remove affected foliage where practical
Rotate crops in future seasons to reduce soil-borne spread
Avoid excess nitrogen fertilization
Follow locally approved plant-protection guidance

3.name: Potato___Late_blight
3.symptoms: Dark, water-soaked lesions spread rapidly on leaves and stems, especially in cool, wet weather.
recommended_actions: Remove and destroy infected plants promptly to limit spread
Avoid overhead irrigation
Ensure good field drainage and airflow
Follow locally approved plant-protection guidance urgently

4.name: Potato___healthy
recommended_actions: Continue regular field monitoring
Maintain proper spacing and drainage
Rotate crops each season for long-term soil health

5.name: Tomato_Bacterial_spot
5.symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked spots appear on leaves and may also affect stems and fruit, sometimes with a yellow halo.
recommended_actions: Remove severely affected leaves
Avoid overhead watering and working with wet plants
Improve air circulation around plants
Follow locally approved plant-protection guidance

6.name: Tomato_Early_blight
6.symptoms: Brown or dark concentric-ring lesions may appear on the lower/older leaves first.
recommended_actions: Remove severely affected leaves
Improve air circulation around plants
Avoid excessive leaf wetness by watering at the base
Monitor nearby plants for spread
Follow locally approved plant-protection guidance

7.name: Tomato_Late_blight
7.symptoms: Water-soaked, dark green to brown patches spread quickly on leaves, often with a pale green border.
recommended_actions: Remove and destroy infected plant material promptly
Avoid overhead watering, especially in the evening
Ensure good spacing and airflow between plants
Act quickly, as this disease can spread rapidly in humid conditions
Follow locally approved plant-protection guidance

8.name: Tomato_Leaf_Mold
8.symptoms: Pale green or yellow spots appear on the upper leaf surface, with an olive-green to grayish mold visible on the underside, usually in humid conditions.
recommended_actions: Improve ventilation and reduce humidity around plants
Avoid overhead watering
Remove and destroy affected leaves
Follow locally approved plant-protection guidance

9.name: Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot
9.symptoms: Small, circular spots with dark borders and light gray centers appear, usually starting on lower leaves.
recommended_actions: Remove and destroy affected lower leaves
Avoid overhead watering
Improve air circulation around plants
Follow locally approved plant-protection guidance

10.name: Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_mite
10.symptoms: Fine yellow speckling or stippling appears on leaves, sometimes with fine webbing visible on the underside in heavy infestations.
recommended_actions: Inspect the underside of leaves closely for tiny mites
Increase humidity around plants where practical, as mites favor hot, dry conditions
Encourage natural predators where possible
Follow locally approved pest management guidance for severe infestations

11.name: Tomato__Target_Spot
11.symptoms: Brown lesions with concentric rings (target-like pattern) appear on leaves and can also affect stems and fruit.
recommended_actions: Remove severely affected leaves
Improve air circulation and reduce leaf wetness
Monitor nearby plants for spread
Follow locally approved plant-protection guidance

12.name: Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus
12.symptoms: Leaves become small, curled upward, and yellow, often with stunted overall plant growth. Commonly spread by whiteflies.
recommended_actions: Remove and destroy severely infected plants to reduce spread
Manage whitefly populations, as they transmit this virus
Avoid working between healthy and infected plants without cleaning tools
Follow locally approved pest and disease management guidance

13.name: Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus
13.symptoms: Leaves show a mottled light and dark green mosaic pattern, and may be misshapen or slightly curled, with possible stunted growth.
recommended_actions: Remove and destroy severely infected plants
Wash hands and disinfect tools between handling plants
Avoid tobacco use near plants, as the virus can spread via contact
Follow locally approved plant-protection guidance

14.name: Tomato_healthy
recommended_actions: Continue regular monitoring
Maintain consistent watering and balanced fertilization
Check both sides of leaves periodically for pests
